display.purpose: The single page-level heading of a console page, e.g. "Devices". Never more than one per page.

headline.purpose: Field-name labels inside device cards ("User", "Platform", "CPU"). Weight 500, never bold.

title.purpose: Device names, card values, dropdown items — the console's default text size.

body.purpose: Running text and control labels at the console's default size.

label.purpose: Navigation links, muted metadata, form labels and small buttons.

shadows.name: floating-prompt
shadows.purpose: The viewer's modal prompt only — the one element that physically floats over the remote screen.

shadows.name: error-strip
shadows.purpose: The Blazor error bar only, anchored to the bottom of the viewport.

motion.name: menu-toggle
motion.purpose: The viewer's menu button rotating its icon 180° when the menu opens.

motion.name: bar-expand
motion.purpose: The viewer's horizontal button bar expanding from height 0 to auto.

motion.name: popup-menu
motion.purpose: Viewer popup menus opening with their 10px padding.

motion.name: toast-message
motion.purpose: Viewer toast notifications sliding out to the right after a 2s delay.

motion.name: field-focus
motion.purpose: Viewer inputs transitioning their border to white on focus.

motion.name: bootstrap-control
motion.purpose: Bootstrap's own control transitions, inherited by every console component.

narrative.overview:
Remotely is a room with one bright thing in it. A technician opens the console, finds the machine that is in trouble, and opens it; from that moment the remote screen is the only object in the room that matters, and every piece of interface around it is instrumentation — a switch, a readout, a way out. The system is built around that one relationship, and it shows in the code: the viewer gives the remote canvas the entire viewport (#workAreaGrid is a fixed inset-0 grid with grid-template-rows: auto 1fr), while the console stays a quiet directory of devices waiting to be chosen.

Two surfaces, one product, two deliberately different manners. The operator console is a Bootstrap 5.3.2 application wearing a Bootswatch theme (Darkly for dark, Yeti for light) — soft 4–6px radii, tonal grey layering, Lato. The remote viewer is hand-written CSS with no framework at all — square 0px controls, hard 1px borders, Lucida Sans, and a single electric accent that only ever appears on the connect and toggle affordances. The console is furniture; the viewer is an instrument. The difference is not drift — it is the difference between a waiting room and the console of a machine.

The governing personality is strictly functional: every element serves the session. Nothing in either surface is decorative. The console has no shadows, no gradients, no illustrations — depth is carried entirely by three greys (#222 canvas → #303030 card → #444 border) and by 1px borders. The viewer has exactly one shadow in the entire system, on the one element that genuinely floats (.modal-prompt). Color is used as signal, never as mood: the console's slate blue marks the primary action, the viewer's Signal Cyan marks the one thing you can act on, and crimson appears once, on the button that ends the session. Where the system is incomplete, it says so plainly — the viewer's light theme is a TODO in Server/Pages/Viewer.cshtml.cs:42 — and where the console drifted, it was corrected rather than excused: site.css no longer declares a font or a link colour that the theme overrides, the sidebar's steelblue gradient is gone, and every console colour now comes from one token layer (--rm-*) shared by both themes.
keyCharacteristics: The remote screen owns the viewport; all chrome floats over it as a thin, square-edged overlay.
Two type systems with different jobs: Lato for the console's readability, Lucida Sans for the viewer's deliberate plainness.
Zero decorative color, zero ornament, zero resting shadows.
One accent per surface, reserved for action: Signal Cyan in the viewer, slate blue in the console.
Radii are a vocabulary, not a gradient: a single 6px in the console, 5px on floating panels, 0px on viewer controls.

rules.name: The Signal Cyan Rule
rules.body: Signal Cyan is reserved for the connect and toggle affordances in the viewer. It is never used for decoration, for data, for hover states on other elements, or anywhere in the console. Its rarity is the point.

rules.name: The Three-Grey Rule
rules.body: The console's depth comes from exactly three greys — #222, #303030, #444 — plus a 1px border. Introducing a fourth surface tone is a change to the system, not a style choice.

rules.name: The Cascade Rule
rules.body: The theme stylesheet is loaded after site.css, so any declaration in site.css that the theme also sets is dead. The file used to declare font-family: 'Helvetica Neue' on html, body and a { color: #0366d6 } while the rendered console used Lato and theme-coloured links; both declarations are now deleted rather than left to be overridden. Verify against computed styles in the running app, never against the source file.

rules.name: The One-Hue Rule
rules.body: The console has one chromatic family — slate blue — plus status colours. Green means online and nothing else, so links are the accent, never green: a green link reads as a status. Yellow means outdated agent, red means destructive. A new colour must be a signal or it does not ship.

rules.name: The Token Rule
rules.body: Every colour the console paints comes from a --rm-* token declared in Server/wwwroot/css/Themes/*.custom.css (dark: darkly.custom.css, light: yeti.custom.css). A raw hex value in a component rule is drift waiting to happen: it will not survive a theme switch. Both themes must declare the same token names.

rules.name: The Two-Stacks Rule
rules.body: The console and the viewer keep separate type systems. Moving Lato into the viewer, or Lucida Sans into the console, merges two surfaces that are deliberately unlike each other.

rules.name: The Weight-500 Rule
rules.body: In the console, hierarchy is carried by size and by weight 500 — never by bold 700, never by color alone. Weight 300 and 400 are the default in the viewer.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. If a new element needs to be distinguished from its neighbors, give it a different tone or a 1px border. A shadow is a last resort and is reserved for something that physically floats over the remote screen.

rules.name: The One Vocabulary Rule
rules.body: Never mix radii within a surface. The console has exactly one radius, 6px, enforced by overriding --bs-border-radius, --bs-border-radius-sm and --bs-border-radius-lg in both themes — a 6px button next to a 4px button in the console is a bug, and so is a rounded button in the viewer.

dos: Do let the remote screen occupy the whole viewport in the viewer, and float the chrome above it.
Do keep the console's depth in the three greys (#222 / #303030 / #444) and 1px borders.
Do take every console colour from a --rm-* token, and declare the same token in both themes.
Do reserve Signal Cyan for the connect and toggle affordances, and slate blue #375a7f for the console's primary action.
Do verify a change against computed styles in the running app — the theme stylesheet loads after site.css and overrides it.
Do keep every control in the viewer at 40px height so the target size stays constant across the toolbar.
Do use Bootstrap's dense vocabulary (table-sm, striped, hover, thead.table-light, btn-sm) for tabular console data instead of inventing a table style.
Do use Lato in the console and Lucida Sans in the viewer, and not the other way round.
donts: Don't add a shadow to a resting surface. The only shadow belongs to the floating prompt.
Don't introduce a second accent color in either surface, and don't carry Signal Cyan into the console.
Don't use green for anything but "online" — a green link reads as a status, not an action.
Don't round a viewer control, mix two radii in the console, or soften a square edge.
Don't decorate, illustrate, or add an empty state that isn't about a device or a session.
Don't assume the viewer has a light theme; Server/Pages/Viewer.cshtml.cs:42 hard-codes dark with a TODO.
Don't declare a colour in site.css that the theme also sets — it is dead code by construction; the console's colours belong to the --rm-* tokens.
